Working with your BDHS microdata

Source: vignettes/microdata.Rmd
microdata.Rmd
library(bdhs)

Why bdhs does not ship the microdata

The DHS Program gives respondent-level data free of charge to registered researchers. Its terms of use say the data must not be passed on to others or redistributed “directly or within any tool”. So bdhs never bundles, uploads or shares microdata, and you should keep your files somewhere private: not in a public GitHub repository and preferably not in a synced cloud folder.

Getting access is quick:

  1. Create an account at https://dhsprogram.com/data/new-user-registration.cfm.
  2. Describe your research project and request the Bangladesh surveys.
  3. Once approved, download the datasets. The Stata format (.DTA, in files like BDIR81DT.ZIP) is recommended because it keeps all variable and value labels.

Analyses published from BDHS data must cite the survey’s final report. The Bangladesh conditions of use also ask for a copy of each publication to be sent to the NIPORT library.

What exists

bdhs_inventory() lists every dataset the DHS Program distributes for Bangladesh and marks which ones you already have:

bdhs_inventory()

The main recode files are:

bdhs_recodes()[1:10, ]
#>    recode                                     name
#> 1      IR              Individual (women's) Recode
#> 2      MR                             Men's Recode
#> 3      KR                        Children's Recode
#> 4      BR                            Births Recode
#> 5      HR                         Household Recode
#> 6      PR                  Household Member Recode
#> 7      CR                          Couples' Recode
#> 8      GR                       Pregnancies Recode
#> 9      NR      Pregnancy and Postnatal Care Recode
#> 10     HW Height and Weight (WHO Growth Standards)
#>                                         unit family
#> 1                                      Woman    DHS
#> 2                                        Man    DHS
#> 3  Child under 5 (born to interviewed women)    DHS
#> 4                 Birth (full birth history)    DHS
#> 5                                  Household    DHS
#> 6                           Household member    DHS
#> 7                                     Couple    DHS
#> 8              Pregnancy (pregnancy history)    DHS
#> 9                           Recent pregnancy    DHS
#> 10               Child measured in household    DHS

Not every recode exists for every round. For example, men were last interviewed in 2011, and the pregnancy (GR) and postnatal care (NR) recodes are new in 2022.

Importing your downloads

Point bdhs_import() at the files, zips or folders you downloaded.

bdhs_import("~/Downloads/BDHS")

bdhs_import() does the following:

  • Recognises DHS files by name (BDIR81FL.DTA), inside zips (BDIR81DT.ZIP), with prefixes (2022BDPR81FL.DTA), and even when you renamed them (BDHS2018KR.DTA). In that case it checks the file’s contents.
  • Skips files that are not original DHS recodes, such as your own merged or appended datasets.
  • Stores a fast copy in the bdhs data directory. With the arrow package installed this is a column-oriented copy, so reading a few variables from a 5,000-column file is quick. Use copy = FALSE to leave files where they are and only register them.
  • Warns if the data directory is inside a git repository or a cloud-sync folder.

The data directory defaults to tools::R_user_dir("bdhs", "data"). Use bdhs_data_dir("path") to change it for the session, or set the BDHS_DATA_DIR environment variable in your .Renviron to change it for good. bdhs_sitrep() summarises your setup.

A complete example with synthetic files

The chunk below runs the full workflow on synthetic files written to a temporary folder, so you can see each step without real data.

# A temporary data directory and some fake DHS files. Both the option and
# the environment variable are set, so your own store is never touched.
store <- file.path(tempdir(), "bdhs-store")
old_opt <- options(bdhs.data_dir = store)
old_env <- Sys.getenv("BDHS_DATA_DIR", unset = NA)
Sys.setenv(BDHS_DATA_DIR = store)

downloads <- file.path(tempdir(), "downloads")
dir.create(downloads, showWarnings = FALSE)
haven::write_dta(bdhs_simulate(2022, "IR"), file.path(downloads, "BDIR81FL.DTA"))
haven::write_dta(bdhs_simulate(2022, "KR"), file.path(downloads, "BDKR81FL.DTA"))
haven::write_dta(bdhs_simulate(2017, "HR"), file.path(downloads, "BDHS2018HR.DTA"))
bdhs_import(downloads)
#> ✔ Imported 3 datasets into /tmp/RtmpMxW3oG/bdhs-store:
#> • BD2017DHS HR (BDHR7RFL): stored as Parquet, 600 rows x 18 variables
#> • BD2022DHS IR (BDIR81FL): stored as Parquet, 552 rows x 116 variables
#> • BD2022DHS KR (BDKR81FL): stored as Parquet, 296 rows x 49 variables
ir <- bdhs_read(2022, "IR", vars = c("v012", "v106", "v313"))
ir
#> # A tibble: 552 × 21
#>    caseid     v000   v001  v002   v005  v003  v007  v021 v022    v023    v024   
#>    <chr>      <chr> <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl+l> <dbl+l> <dbl+l>

#>  3 "       1… BD8       1     4 744251     2  2022     1 1 [bar… 1 [bar… 1 [bar…

When you ask for specific variables, bdhs_read() always adds the identifiers and design variables (cluster, strata, weight, region, residence and the all-woman factors). That way the result can go straight into bdhs_design() or bdhs_merge(). Use labels = "factor" to get factors instead of labelled numbers.

Downloading with your DHS account (experimental)

bdhs_download() can log in to the DHS website with your account and fetch files directly:

bdhs_download(2022, c("IR", "KR"), email = "you@university.edu", project = "Your project title")

Your password is never stored by bdhs. It is read from the system keyring (keyring package, service "bdhs-dhs"), the DHS_PASSWORD environment variable, or an interactive prompt. The DHS website can change without notice, so if the downloader fails, download the files in your browser and use bdhs_import().

Reading one-off files

bdhs_read_file() reads any DHS file without registering it and applies the same conventions: lower-case names, preserved labels and detected survey and recode.

pr <- bdhs_read_file("~/Downloads/BDPR81FL.DTA", vars = c("hv104", "hv105"))
